what: same-item retrieval quality: a model-independent target for comparing embedders

task.relevant: other passages of the probe's own Zotero item, at least 3 chunks away
task.excluded_from_candidates: the probe's own item's passages within 3 chunks of it
task.why_the_gap: the chunker overlaps by 150 characters, so adjacent chunks share text outright and any embedder retrieves them; without the gap this measures near-duplicate detection and saturates

caveats: Same-item relatedness is document-level topical coherence, not query-to-answer relevance. This proxy can show a model is too weak; it cannot certify one is good enough for a user’s real questions.
Recall is divided by min(relevant, topk), so an item with more than topk eligible siblings is not penalised for the ones that cannot fit.
Comparing two DIFFERENT models here conflates dimension with architecture, size and training data. Only the widths WITHIN one Matryoshka model isolate dimension.

POOLING VERIFIED (2026-08-29, ticket 0421). bge-small-en-v1.5 pools with cls, and this run's bge.f32 slab was cls-pooled: measured, not inferred. Re-embedding the same passages at each pooling mode and scoring against the slab's own rows gives cosine 1,000000 on every row at cls against a 0,912731 median at mean (bench/results/0421-slab-pooling/bge.json). The control discriminates in the opposite direction -- minilm384.f32 reads 1,000000 at mean and 0,440759 median at cls (minilm-control.json) -- so the verdict rests on a wide gap rather than a threshold. The figure below therefore stands: it is not understated by the hardcoded pooling: 'mean' that every transformers.js driver passed until 0421. The comparison is row-exact because passages.items, bge.f32.items and nomic.f32.items are md5-identical (a677dcb1), so row i of the slab is line i of the corpus. Recorded because the missing sibling .meta.json makes this artifact look doubtful and it is not: the absence names which tool wrote the slab, not whether the pooling was right, and meta never tracked chronology anyway (minilm384.f32 has none while the earlier qwen06b.f32 does). The sibling task-recall.json is likewise sound; its Qwen3 arm carries embed_corpus.py's meta.
